findings.title: --tempo / analyzeTempo drop the first beat when the audio starts on the beat; the snippet then opens a beat (or a whole bar) late and describes an intro that does not exist
findings.failure_scenario: A track whose first kick sits at t ≈ 0 (trimmed loop, cue, stock track that starts on the 1): `node lv.mjs --tempo track.wav`. The measured phase comes out a few ms NEGATIVE (e.g. −1 ms), `ph0 = ((toSec(ph) % beat) + beat) % beat` wraps it to ~0.498, and the loop at line 604 starts at ph0, so the beat at ~0 is never emitted even though the `- beat/4` slack on the same line was written to allow it. Result: first beat 0.4986 s instead of 0; with a clear bar accent `start` becomes 1.9985 instead of 0 (the film opens a full bar into the track and 2 s of a 12 s file are lost), and the `alternative` line claims `# keeps the 1.9985 s intro` for a file with no intro. The same wrong 'first beat 0.496 s' prints on the contact sheet and breakdown.md of a reel whose audio starts on a beat.
findings.evidence: Synthetic kick at 120 BPM starting at offset t0 (work/TOOL/syn/k_<t0>.wav): t0=0 → 'first beat 0.4982', t0=0.002 → 'first beat 0.4987', t0=0.005 → 'first beat 0.0015' (correct), 0.01/0.02/0.03 correct. So it is a ±3 ms coin flip for any beat at the file start. Accented-bar file work/TOOL/syn/acc0.wav (loud kick on beat 1 of each 2 s bar, starting at 0): output 'first beat 0.4986 s · first downbeat 1.9985 s (bar confidence 0.293)', snippet 'start: 1.9985, downbeat: 0', alt 'start: 0, downbeat: 1.9985 # keeps the 1.9985 s intro'. bar0.wav and a kick-at-0 video (syn/syn_onbeat.mp4, sheet shows 'first beat 0.496 s') behave the same. I patched a copy (work/TOOL/skill-q) with `for (let s = ph0 - beat; …) … beats.push(r4(Math.max(0, s)))`: acc0 → first beat 0 / downbeat 0 (correct), but work/TOOL/syn/padintro.wav (2 s pad, drums from 2.0) regresses to downbeat 0 because the pad's start transient scores as an accent — so the fix needs an onset-strength check.
findings.suggested_fix: Start the grid one beat earlier (`s = ph0 - beat`) but keep a beat before ph0 only when the onset strength at it is comparable to the other beats (a bare music-start transient from silence must not count), clamp `firstBeat`/`start` to ≥ 0, and only emit the 'keeps the intro' alternative when there is real pre-beat material (start ≥ ~0.25 s AND the start is a first-beat/downbeat found after an onset-free stretch).

findings.title: The 'ready' music: snippet from --tempo is invalid or wrong YAML for ordinary track file names
findings.failure_scenario: `lv.mjs --tempo "Song Title [NCS Release].mp3"` (or a name with a comma, ': ', ' #', { or }) prints `music: {style: track, file: assets/Song Title [NCS Release].mp3, bpm: …}` — an unquoted scalar inside a flow mapping. Pasting it into beats.yaml makes the whole file fail to parse at --grid ('beats.yaml is not valid YAML …'), or silently truncates the path at ' #'. Same for the `alternative` line (1029).
findings.evidence: work/TOOL/syn/"Artist, Other - Track: Remix [v2] #1.wav" → snippet `file: assets/Artist, Other - Track: Remix [v2] #1.wav`; yaml.parse of that line: 'Unexpected flow-seq-start at node end at line 1, column 65'. A name 'Hey #1 Hit.wav' fails with 'Flow map in block collection must be sufficiently indented…'. Names with only spaces/parentheses ('Artist - Other (Official Video) 2024.wav') parse fine, so it bites only on , [ ] { } #, ': '.
findings.suggested_fix: Emit the path with JSON.stringify (`file: "assets/…"`) in both snippet lines, or quote only when /[,\[\]{}#:]|^\s|\s$/ matches.

findings.title: --breakdown output folder collides for CJK-only, long, or similarly-named references; the second run silently overwrites the first (including its filled-in breakdown.md)
findings.failure_scenario: GUIDE prescribes `--breakdown` once per reference (2–3 references per brief) into `DIR/reference/<name>/`. `referenceDir` uses slugify(), which strips every non-ASCII letter, lower-cases, and truncates to 40 chars; `|| 'reel'` is dead code because slugify itself returns 'launch-video' for an empty result. So `参考视频.mp4` and `对标.mp4` both land in reference/launch-video/; `Higgsfield AI product launch reel for Instagram - version 1.mp4` and `… version 2.mp4` both land in reference/higgsfield-ai-product-launch-reel-for-in/; 'Reel A.mp4' vs 'reel_a.mp4' collide too. The second run deletes the first one's sheets, thumbs, breakdown.json/md and beats-draft.yaml (lines 990–991) with no warning. The draft slug has the same problem ('ref-launch-video').
findings.evidence: work/TOOL: `lv.mjs --job cjk --breakdown syn/参考视频.mp4` then `--breakdown syn/对标.mp4` → only `cjk/reference/launch-video/` exists, breakdown.json source.name = 对标.mp4. Long names: `jobs/coll/reference/` holds a single folder 'higgsfield-ai-product-launch-reel-for-in' after two runs on different files.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the folder name unique per source: slug + short hash of the resolved path (or of name+size), or refuse/warn when the target folder's breakdown.json has a different source.file. Fall back to a transliteration or the first characters of the raw name when the slug is empty.

findings.title: Gradual transitions are missed on real footage: a cross-dissolve is not found at all, and a dip to black (fade-out immediately followed by fade-in) is reported as ONE shot
findings.failure_scenario: GUIDE's 'Reading it' lists `dissolve` and `fade (a dip)` as detected transitions. On real moving footage: (a) the blend test at line 444 (`m0.r > .2*raw …`) compares the middle frame with a mix of frames k±h (h up to 24 frames); when either picture moves inside that window the residual exceeds 20 % and every candidate is rejected, so a 0.5 s cross-dissolve between two real clips yields no cut and no event. (b) For a dip with no black hold (fade-out ends on the frame where the fade-in starts) the fade-in candidate is rejected by the 'bounded' test at line 441 (the incoming picture keeps moving, so the quiet-outside condition fails) and the two windows touch at the black frame, which the overlap test at line 455 (`x.a <= g.b && x.b >= g.a`) would also drop. Only the fade-out is reported, as an in-shot event: 'N shots' undercounts and beats-draft.yaml lacks the shot. The workflow only tells the reader to merge OVER-split shots, so the miss is not surfaced.
findings.evidence: Real clips (kling-15s + running short video from ~/Downloads, read-only), 0.5 s xfade → work/TOOL/syn/realdiss.mp4: 1 shot, no events. Same clips with fade=out/fade=in back to back → syn/realdip.mp4: 1 shot, events only 'fade-in 4–4.6 s'. Synthetic gradients→testsrc2 and testsrc2→mandelbrot dips (syn/dip.mp4, dip2.mp4, dip3.mp4): 1 shot + 'fade-out 2.4–3.0 s'. With BD_DEBUG-style instrumentation on a patched copy, reason counts for realdiss were reject-5 (blend residual) 57×, reject-4 (bounded) 5×, reject-3 2×; relaxing the overlap test alone only fixed the variant with a 0.3 s black hold (syn/dip5.mp4 → 'fade' cut at 3.0). A dip WITH a black hold already comes out as a dissolve+fade-in pair, so only the no-hold dip and the moving-footage dissolve are lost.
findings.suggested_fix: Measure the dissolve against its own start/end frames (locate the ramp from the per-frame difference profile and blend frames at the ramp edges, not at ±h), let adjacent fade-out/fade-in windows touch, and relax the 'bounded' test when the ends are near-uniform (black/white). Until then say in GUIDE Limits that dissolves/dips over moving footage are usually missed, and add 'two different scenes inside one shot' as a thing to look for on the sheets.

findings.failure_scenario: `lv.mjs --init --kit film` then `--film --aspect 16x9` ends 'QA FAILED (2)'. (1) cut name→hook: change 30.85 vs neighbours ≤ 32.20 (0.96×). (3) content, frame 465 (REPORTS lists only '290–307'): the first frame of `ask` (theme dark, no bg, words overlay fading in from at: 0) is the bare dark background (0 differing thumbnail px). The sentences 'It runs as is' in film.yaml/reel.yaml header comments read as promising a QA-clean film, but only --grid/--storyboard are true.

Fix tried on copies of the rendered job: (a) bg on `hook` only (`bg: assets/placeholder-clip-1.svg`, `--film --aspect 16x9 --range 290,464`, jobs/film-fix): cut becomes 150.38 (4.67×) PASS but content still FAILs at frame 465. Reel starter: QA PASSED (13 checks) at 16x9 and 9x16, `--clips s1,s4 --alpha` PASS.

findings.title: Valueless --min-shot / --per-page are silently coerced to 1 (and flag errors exit 1, not 2)
findings.failure_scenario: `lv.mjs --job D --breakdown reel.mp4 --min-shot` (value forgotten) or `--per-page`: common.mjs arg() returns `true` for a flag with no value, and breakdown.mjs:890 does Number(true)=1, which passes the 0–5 / 1–40 checks. So --min-shot becomes 1 s (cuts closer than 1 s are merged away: 6 shots → 5) and --per-page becomes 1 shot per sheet (6 sheet PNGs). `--threshold` with no value only errors by accident (1 is outside 0–1). `--fps` in the same CLI is rejected with exit 2, but the breakdown parameter errors (and file-not-found) exit 1.
findings.evidence: work/TOOL: `lv.mjs --job e1 --breakdown syn/syn_onbeat.mp4 --min-shot` → '5 shots … 4/4 cuts' (6 shots / 5 cuts without the flag); `--per-page` → 'sheet-01.png … sheet-06.png'; `--threshold` → error 'must be between 0 and 1' rc=1.
findings.suggested_fix: In lv.mjs (and the standalone CLI) treat `true` from arg() as 'missing value' for numeric options and die(…, 2) with the flag name; use exit 2 for parameter errors like --fps does.

findings.title: Timecodes are wrong by frames at 29.97 / 23.976 (NTSC) source rates
findings.failure_scenario: For a CFR 29.97 source `fr = Math.round(fps)` = 30 and timecode(t, 30) computes round(t*30) from SECONDS, which counts 1.001× too many frames. The sheet/breakdown.md promise 'MM:SS:FF at the source rate' for finding a cut in an editor, but at 60 s the cut at frame 1800 shows 01:00:02 (non-drop timecode would be 01:00:00); the error grows 1 frame per ~33 s (23.976: ~1 frame per 42 s). The label on thumbnails ('+2f 01:00:04') inherits it.
findings.evidence: work/TOOL/syn/ntsc.mp4 (30000/1001, cut at frame 1800, 2100 frames): breakdown.json shots[1].startFrame 1800, tcIn '01:00:02'; last shot tcOut '01:10:02' for frame 2100 (expected 01:10:00).
findings.suggested_fix: For non-VFR sources derive the timecode from the decode frame index (a / fr, a % fr; startFrame is already stored) instead of from seconds, or document that the TC is seconds×rate.

findings.title: --init --kit … --title writes YAML-1.2 booleans/null for names like True/Null and keeps 'Product' elsewhere; CJK titles get monogram 'P'
findings.failure_scenario: The kit path edits the starter with a regex and the helper `y()` leaves /^[A-Za-z][\w .'-]*$/ unquoted, so `--title True` writes `name: True` (boolean true) and `--title Null` writes `name: Null` (null). spec.mjs then takes brand.name = 'true' (String(true)) or falls back to the title 'Null launch film' (which shows in the lockup). findings.evidence: work/TOOL/inits/True_reel/beats.yaml: yaml.parse → brand.name true (boolean); Null_film → null; 阿里云 → mono: P. The non-kit --init path uses YAML.parseDocument and quotes correctly.
findings.suggested_fix: Use YAML.stringify(value) for the replaced scalars (or quote anything matching /^(true|false|null|yes|no|on|off|~)$/i); fall back to the first character of the title for mono; print 'copy in the shots still says Product — find/replace it' after --init --kit --title.

findings.title: Engine camera field `move: [x, y]` collides with the media block's documented Ken Burns param `move: in|out|left|right|none`
findings.failure_scenario: An existing job with `{block: media, src: assets/pic.jpg, move: left}` (the documented media param: GUIDE.md:151 table, `lv.mjs --blocks`) now stops at --grid with exit 2 "move must be [x, y], a constant drift…" (every shot is validated for the camera fields). Writing the array form instead passes the spec but media.js:50 reads `s.move || 'in'`, so the array matches none of in/out/left/right/none and the shot gets a static 1.1 scale instead of Ken Burns; the same value also drives the engine camera, so one field means two things. The GUIDE contradicts itself: line 151 lists `move` as a media param, line 213 says the engine owns `move` on every shot.
findings.evidence: Job /Users/bytedance/Downloads/Design-AutoPilot-stable/qa/launch-video-skill-review/work/ENG/j2/beats.yaml (two media shots, `move: left` and `move: out`, otherwise valid). `node pre/video/lv.mjs --job j2 --grid` → rc=0, timeline printed. `node skill/video/lv.mjs --job j2 --grid` (snapshot copy) → rc=2: "shots[0] (a): move must be [x, y]… (got \"left\")" and the same for shots[1]. grep of every pre block shows media is the only built-in whose param collides with zoom/focus/offset/pan/move/drift (wall's string `drift` is special-cased; media's `move` is not). No sample job in ~/Downloads/launch-videos happens to use media `move`, which is why the regression runs did not see it. lib/sheet.mjs:67 also still describes media with `s.move`.
findings.suggested_fix: Key the camera field by type: in spec.mjs skip camera validation of `move` when the value is a string (or when block is media), and in runtime.js make hasView/viewFor/camFields treat `move` as a camera field only when Array.isArray(s.move) (or per-aspect map of arrays). Better: rename the camera field (e.g. `glide:`) and keep media's `move` untouched. Update GUIDE.md:213 accordingly and add a media `move: left` job to the regression set.

findings.title: A truncated or part-corrupt JPEG/PNG used as bg passes --grid, the stage build and film QA, and ships a half-empty frame — the 'truncated download' case the code comment claims to refuse
findings.failure_scenario: The comment at runtime.js:347 says an undecodable file ("a truncated download, an HTML page or a HEIC saved as .jpg") stops the build. Chrome's img.decode() resolves for a partially decodable raster, imageProblem() only sniffs the first 4096 bytes, so a bg image cut off mid-download renders the top part of the picture and the rest as the dark underlay plus the mirrored strip. Film QA passes because the content reference deliberately hides footage.
findings.evidence: work/ENG/jt_trunc.jpg and jt_trunc.png (work/ENG/j4/assets/pic.jpg / pic.png cut at 50% of their bytes, used as `bg:` on a headline shot) and work/ENG/jb (assets/corrupt.png = 400 bytes of mid-IDAT XORed). `lv.mjs --grid` rc=0 for all; t_open.mjs: stage builds with no error; screenshots jt_trunc.jpg.png, jt_trunc.png.png and jb_corrupt.png show the bottom ~47% of the frame as flat dark. `lv.mjs --job jt_trunc.png --film --aspect 16x9` → "QA PASSED (9 checks)" (jt.film.log). A fully broken SVG is caught ("bg assets/broken.svg could not be decoded as an image"), so only partial decodes slip through.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend imageProblem() with tail checks: JPEG must end FFD9 (ignoring trailing zero padding), PNG must end with an IEND chunk (ideally walk chunks and CRC them), WebP RIFF size must equal file size − 8, GIF must end 0x3B. Optionally, at build, draw each decoded bg/img to a canvas and refuse an image whose last row is fully transparent or uniform grey. Fix the runtime.js:347 comment and the GUIDE.md:567 sentence to say what is actually caught.

findings.title: The mirror-extended bg plate has 1 px dark seam lines at the tile joins whenever camera × Ken Burns scale is below 1 (every bg shot's first ~3 frames, ~8 at film start, longer with bgMove: none)
findings.failure_scenario: buildFoot lays nine abutting <image> tiles. When the shot's total scale is below 1 the tile boundaries fall inside the frame at fractional pixel positions; the two antialiased edges do not add to full coverage and the near-black underlay (C.dark) shows through as a 1 px line, 15–40/255 darker than the picture (a 'hard edge', exactly what the mirror extension is meant to avoid). It happens at the opening (first shot enters at s −0.06), on the default cut entrance (s −0.04 × Ken Burns 1.02 < 1 for ~3 frames = 6 frames at 60 fps, seams 20→3 px inside each edge), on zoom-in/blur/whip entrances, and for ~13 frames with bgMove: none.

findings.title: QA `whoosh` check false-fails ~5% of tunnel and glitch cuts (and ~2% of whip/drift): noise-driven peak lands >12 ms from the cut
findings.failure_scenario: A normal film with a `tunnel` or `glitch` exit gets `FAIL whoosh ...` purely from where its cut falls relative to the sample grid; the user cannot fix it except by nudging timing, and GUIDE says never ship a FAIL / never loosen a threshold. A film with 6 same-type cuts fails QA about a quarter of the time.
findings.evidence: Real pipeline (loadSpec -> compile -> buildAudio -> the exact `peak()` from qa.mjs:218 on out/audio/whoosh.wav), 24 films x 6 cuts each at varied BPM/lengths (script work/LIB/aud2/run.mjs <out>): tunnel 7/144 cuts > 12 ms (max 25 ms), 6/24 films FAIL; glitch 8/144 (max 21 ms), 7/24 films FAIL; whip-left 3/144 (max 13 ms), 3/24 films; drift-up 2/144; smear-left and flash 0/144. Engine-only sweep over 400 cut times (work/LIB/aud/sweep.mjs): tunnel 25/400 > 12 ms, glitch 6/400, whip 4/400; mean offset is -3 to -4 ms (peak found early). Deterministic failing examples: `cp work/LIB/aud2/fail-tunnel.yaml work/LIB/aud3/beats.yaml; node work/LIB/aud3/one.mjs` -> `1.417->1.416, 2.983->2.968 ... worst 15 ms -> FAIL`; same for fail-glitch.yaml (bpm 116, 15 ms). Removing the low-end share does not cure it (tunnel low=0: still 11/300), so the cause is the long flat u^2.6 rise (tunnel pre .62 s, tail .09) plus random band-pass noise inside the 20 ms RMS window, not the coded peak time. The old `whoosh` already had ~1% tail risk; sweep()/glitch() (voices.mjs:136-163, audio.mjs:97-107) make it 5%.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the peak deterministic instead of widening the 12 ms tolerance: synthesise the whoosh from a smooth, noise-free amplitude envelope (e.g. shape an envelope-normalised noise, or add a short deterministic thump/click exactly at tp), force the glitch gate open for +/-25 ms around tp, and/or have QA measure on a smoothed or high-passed stem. Add a QA self-test that sweeps tp over 300 positions per type and asserts 0 offsets > 12 ms.

Per-frame YAVG around the cut (ffmpeg tblend on k1/out/main/16x9/frames): 281:18.1, 283:22.8, 285:22.0, 287:25.5, 288:28.1, 289:32.2, 290(cut):30.8, 291:0.05 - the pre-cut side is the through zoom, the post-cut side is a bare brand background. Verified fix without touching thresholds (work/LIB/k1b, range re-render of hook+ask): setting `bg: assets/placeholder-clip-1.svg` on hook and `bg: assets/placeholder-clip-2.svg` on ask (the placeholder SVGs are already copied by --init) gives `PASS cut name->hook ... 150.38 vs 32.20 (4.67x)` and `PASS content ... min 262 differing thumbnail px`. Sources: engine/blocks/type.js:9 (`thr` = through frames) and :31; qa.mjs:166 treats every `out: cut` strictly; templates/film.yaml:34-44, 46-51, 55-62 keep the scenes bg-less.

findings.title: `--tempo` first-beat/phase locks onto offbeat hats and reports confidence 1 (cross-area: breakdown.mjs analysis, ships through the lv.mjs --tempo wiring)
findings.failure_scenario: On a four-on-the-floor pattern (kick on every beat, noise hat on the off-beats at ~-14 dB) `--tempo` prints the right BPM but a first beat half a beat late, with confidence 1 and no warning, and the ready `music:` line puts `start` on the hat. Every cut then lands on the off-beat, 234 ms off at 128 BPM.
findings.evidence: Synthetic tracks (work/LIB/bd/mk.py): kicks at 0.37 s + k*0.46875 s (128 BPM). With hats 0.05 -> first beat 0.3674 (correct). With hats 0.2 (beat128.wav) -> `first beat 0.605`, i.e. 0.37 + beat/2. 90 BPM, kick at 0.5, hats 0.2 -> first beat 0.8351 (kick 0.5 + 0.3351 = half beat). 128 BPM kick at 0.0, hats 0.2 -> 0.2353. Hats 0.5 -> 0.6042 with first downbeat 2.0106. Kick-only tracks (k_only 0.3675, 55 BPM folded to 110, 87.4 and 123.5 BPM fractional, 200 BPM) are correct, and the skill's own keynote music reads on-beat (0.4874 vs grid 0.4839), so the failure needs a hat that is not much weaker than the kick. Cause: the beat phase comes from comb-scoring the summed log-magnitude spectral flux over all bins (breakdown.mjs onsets(), ~526-545, and the comb in analyzeTempo ~569-585), where a broadband hat adds flux in ~250 bins versus a kick's few low bins; the low-band accent is only used to choose the downbeat (~596).
findings.suggested_fix: Estimate phase from a low-band (< ~200 Hz) or kick-weighted novelty (or run the comb on both and prefer the one whose onsets carry more low-band energy), and lower the reported confidence / add a note when the half-beat phase scores within ~15% of the chosen one.
